data_fields.name: tap_commit_window_ms
data_fields.donor_constant: none (a tap acts on press, no window)

best_idea: Decide a touch's meaning on lift and keep the second finger as a camera or cancel rule, so a pinch never fires the first finger's action and any held item is released through the same snap rule as a normal release.
decision_why: The one-finger-primary and two-finger-camera split fits a touch-first client, but the donor acts on press and drops a held node without the snap and overlap rule; commit-on-lift and one shared release path are the fixes.
acceptance: On a 375-wide touch screen, a two-finger pinch that starts on empty ground places nothing; a single tap still acts (a placement appears on lift); a node dropped by a second finger or a cancelled touch lands on the normal grid rule, and a drop onto an occupied tile returns it to its start. A unit test asserts both.
